doc.name: A — luggage catalogue, spa marble, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: polycarbonate carry-on
Category: luggage
Shot programme: spa marble
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You act as lead photographer and set designer for a luggage catalogue. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the shadow-play silhouette in a spa marble treatment.

SUBJECT. A polycarbonate carry-on. Treat the attached reference as the single source of truth for the product's geometry, proportion, colourway, finish and label typography. Do not redesign, restyle, re-letter or embellish it.

CAMERA. Backlit so the product edge glows and the set falls into shadow. Shoot on a 90mm tilt-shift at f/2.8, framing for a stacked layered composition with three depth planes.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with underlighting from a translucent base panel. Stage the product on or against book-matched marble, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a bleach-bypass look with crushed saturation and lifted contrast. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Reply with a single continuous prompt paragraph. Never explain, never bullet, never wrap it in markdown fences.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
